subject: Medline AI — request for bundled premium support & SFTP integration concession
messages:
From: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@medline.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medline.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal questions — premium support bundle + SFTP integration

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers and cost profile look promising. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of items before we move to an LOI:

- Medline needs premium support (24x7 on-call) included for the first 12 months.
- We also require Redwood to deliver a one-off SFTP-based ingestion integration (customer-managed SFTP -> Redwood ingest) and migration assistance.
- Procurement is asking whether you can bundle onboarding + premium support into a single commercial line and provide a concession (they mentioned 35–40% off list as a target).

Target go-live: Nov 1. We need a clear cost + statement of work and any exceptions to standard SLAs.

Can you share an updated SOW and a ballpark that includes the requested concessions? Attaching our internal integration spec for context (large files, nightly batch).

Thanks — happy to schedule time if that helps.

Ian
Director of Data Platform
Medline AI Health

Attachments: Medline_Integration_Spec_v1.docx (attachment stub)
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@medline.ai>, procurement@medline.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal questions — premium support bundle + SFTP integration

Ian — appreciate the clear ask and timelines.

Short answer: we can include premium support for 12 months and cover an SFTP integration as professional services, but the economics depend on scope. I attached a draft SOW and a preliminary price summary. High-level options:

1) Standard package (no concession): onboarding + 12mo Premium Support + SFTP integration (est. 60 hours) — list $210k.
2) Concession scenario: bundle + 30% one-time discount (requires 24-month reserved commit or an approval from RevOps/Finance) — est. $147k.
3) Aggressive concession (40%): requires exec approval and commitment to a 36-month reserved capacity or a signed LOI with a non-refundable onboarding deposit.

I’ve looped Ben and Marissa to confirm PS hours and to route for escalation/approval. Ben — can you confirm whether RevOps will entertain a 30% concession in exchange for a 24mo commit? Marissa — please advise on integration hours and any risk items we should highlight for execs.

Next steps: if you’re OK, we’ll set a 30-minute call Monday to walk procurement through options and DocuSign timelines.

—Tessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Medline — ask for exec concession (40% ask)

Team — forwarding the ask from Medline. Procurement is pushing hard for a 35–40% concession on the bundled line (onboarding + 12mo Premium Support + SFTP integration). Client timeline is Nov 1.

Key facts:
- Proposed standard list: $210k (one-time onboarding + 12 months of Premium Support + PS hours for integration).
- Medline is pushing for 40% off; they are not yet committing to reserved capacity.
- Integration is customer-managed SFTP; there is potential for corner-case failures and file format normalization work.

Asks:
1) Ben — need RevOps view: will Finance allow a 30% vs 40% concession without a longer-term commit? What approvals do we need for >30%?
2) Marissa — scope confirmation: SFTP migration + nightly batch ingestion; estimate PS effort and any dependencies we should flag in SOW.
3) Priya — if this is a strategic healthcare account, can we prioritize PS scheduling for an Oct onboarding window?

I’ve attached price_summary.xlsx and the draft SOW (Medline_SOW_v3.pdf). Please reply with your recommended concession ceiling and any blocking risks. If we need exec signoff, please specify the approver.

Thanks — Tessa
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Medline — ask for exec concession (40% ask)

Tessa / Ben / Priya — reviewed the integration spec and SOW. Quick notes (redlines inline in the attached SOW):

- Integration hours: baseline 40 hours for the SFTP connector (parsing, normalization, retry logic) + 10 hours migration support = 50 hours total. If Medline has non-standard file formats we should add an allowance (up to 20 hrs) as an addendum.
- Risk: nightly large-file windows increase support overhead; need an SLA carve-out for ingest retry/backfill windows in month 1.
- PS scheduling: we can commit to an Oct onboarding provided the client signs the LOI and provides a dedicated engineering contact.

Commercial recommendation: cap standard concession at 25% without an upfront revenue commit. I can support up to 30% if RevOps confirms a 24mo reserved capacity contract. Anything >30% requires exec approval (RevOps + Head of Revenue). For a 36mo commit we can consider 35–40% but would want an onboarding deposit ($50k) and an explicit SFTP complexity allowance.

If you want, I can summarize for the deal desk — recommend: offer 30% tied to 24mo reserved capacity, attach SOW with the 20-hr complexity addendum, and require LOI + deposit to secure Oct slot.

—Marissa
Director, Professional Services | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Medline_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf

Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Medline — ask for exec concession (40% ask)

Team — thanks for the quick analysis. Summary and recommended path for exec:

- We should present the client with two formal commercial options:
  A) 24mo reserved capacity + one-time onboarding + 12mo Premium Support at 30% concession (final = $147k) — no SLA exceptions beyond standard PS carve-outs.
  B) 36mo reserved capacity + onboarding deposit ($50k) + 35% concession — limited to approved exec signoff (Rishi + Head of Revenue). Includes SFTP baseline (50hrs) and complexity addendum for any custom parsing.

- Risk items to surface to execs: potential additional PS hours if file formats are not as documented; first-30-day support for large nightly windows; requires engineering contact from Medline.

Rishi — can you approve option B for cases where Sales secures a $50k onboarding deposit and a 36mo commit? If yes, I’ll draft the exec approval email for signature and route to Finance. If no, we proceed with option A and position it as our baseline near-term offer.

Ben Carter
